description:
Phase 6e follow-up under epic `026fc832`. 695350fd R0 (commits `0de86fd9..191a69c8`) hit a structural wall on GF(65521)/n=4096: AVX2 u16-mulhi-mullo MAC is arithmetic-bound at ~40 Gop/s (kernel achieves 106% of estimated shuffle-pipe ceiling). fflas's 69.72 Gop/s matches Zen-3 f64 FMA peak (70 GFLOP/s = 2 × 8 lanes × 4.4 GHz) — strongly suggesting fflas uses an f64 GEMM cascade for fp_medium primes. Closing GF(65521)/n=4096 (and improving the Schur-update path for GF(65521) PLE in 68db401b) requires a new f64 cascade kernel for fp_medium, analogous to Route A's f32 cascade for fp_small (which closed GF(251) via the 41096af5 wire-in + 74ba1cdc R1 BLIS restructure). ## Background After 695350fd R0: - GF(65521)/n=4096: 40.25 Gop/s (was 39.78 post-74ba1cdc R1); ratio 1.732 (was 1.753) - The +1.2% improvement landed; the AVX2 u16 ceiling is now well-characterised - fflas uses ~70 Gop/s ≈ Zen3 f64 FMA peak; gf2's u16 path is at 57% of that Architectural pattern: For GF(p) with p ≤ 65521, an f64 cascade represents each element as f64, performs the f64 GEMM (vendor-tuned at near-peak), then reduces mod p via Barrett. This is fflas's approach for medium primes via OpenBLAS's dgemm. **gf2 needs an in-Rust + AVX2 analogue.** Route A is the precedent for fp_small (f32 cascade). The f64 cascade for fp_medium is structurally similar but at f64 precision: - 4 f64 lanes per AVX2 register (vs 8 f32 lanes) - Mantissa: 52 bits (vs 23 for f32) - Max product: p² ≤ 65520² ≈ 2³² → fits in f64 mantissa with k_max ≈ 2²⁰ MACs between reductions - 1 FMA per MAC; reduction every k_max ≈ 1M MACs ## Scope Add a new f64 cascade GEMM kernel for fp_medium primes. Wire it into the existing dispatch chain so `gemm` + `gemm_axpy_into_view` route the new kernel when `(251 < P < 65536) && AVX2_avail && shape_threshold_met`. 1. **New SSOT helper**: `crates/gf2-kernels-simd/src/x86/fp_medium_f64.rs` — AVX2 f64 cascade kernel with BLIS-style MC/KC/NC blocking (apply the 74ba1cdc R1 + 695350fd R0 lessons learned). 2. **Safe wrapper** in `crates/gf2-kernels-simd/src/fp_medium_f64.rs`. 3. **`Fp

` dispatch override** for `P` in (251, 65536) — add `try_simd_gemm_classical_f64` analogue. 4. **Dispatch hook**: extend `gemm` (matrix.rs:2642) + `gemm_axpy_into_view` (matrix.rs:2854, post-40195c09-lift) to call the f64 kernel for medium primes at appropriate sizes. 5. **Threshold tuning** — the f64 cascade has packing overhead; tune the size threshold empirically (likely n ≥ 256 or 512). ## Success Criteria - [hard] GF(65521) at n=4096: ratio gf2/fflas ≤ 1.5× on 5-trial CCX1-pinned bench (flock-guarded via `dev/benchmarks/ccx1-bench-flock.sh`) on the Zen 3 reference host. Reference: 69.72 Gop/s fflas single-thread. - [hard] No regression on existing PASS cells at n ∈ {64, 256, 1024} for all 6 primes (delta ≤ 5%). Baselines: post-695350fd evidence + 74ba1cdc R1 evidence. - [hard] Bit-exact correctness preserved across all primes — proptest sweep at boundary lengths {0, 1, 15, 16, 17, 63, 64, 65}. - [hard] No BLAS dependency. No external linker change. Pure Rust + AVX2. - [hard] Unsafe stays in `gf2-kernels-simd` (no new unsafe in `gf2-core`). - [hard] Evidence doc records pre/post numbers + non-regression sweep + reproducibility commands. - [hard] After landing, 98336ab4 worker re-benches all n=4096 cells with warmup-matched protocol; 98336ab4 closes PASS for all 6 cells (already a follow-on dep). ## Out of scope - Route A / GF(251) — closed by 74ba1cdc R1. - u16 BLIS restructure on the existing fp_medium kernel — 695350fd already landed the +1.2% improvement; further u16 work is bounded by the arithmetic ceiling. - AVX-512 — epic `7f809931`. - BLAS delegation — user-rejected. - Multi-threading — separate epic. - GF(65521) PLE base case — `68db401b` (Phase 6d). The f64 cascade may benefit 68db401b's Schur-update path; coordinate at impl time. ## Notes - Filed session 9 (2026-05-26) per user-approved deferral of 695350fd SC#1. - Reference: 695350fd R0 evidence doc (`dev/bench_results/2026-05-26-695350fd-fp-medium-blis.md` § 9 has the f64 cascade design sketch + µop analysis); 74ba1cdc R1 evidence (Route A f32 cascade precedent). - Estimated effort: 1-2 weeks of focused engineering (similar to 74ba1cdc R1's scope on Route A).
